claims.text: Shielded ZEC → 30+ chains
claims.source: README.md (top): "swapping shielded ZEC for tokens on 30+ chains"; web/src/lib/chainNames.ts lists 35 destination chains

claims.text: Swapping ZEC today means unshielding it first. NEAR Intents can already swap ZEC. But that ZEC is a bridged token: it left the shielded pool for a transparent address first.
claims.source: README.md "The problem": inside NEAR Intents ZEC is the NEP-141 token nep141:zec.omft.near (1Click token list, 2026-11-13), not shielded ZEC; Cloakroom paper quote on routes through a transparent address

claims.text: The ZEC stays shielded the whole way.
claims.source: README.md "The problem": "Zecret keeps the ZEC in the shielded pool for the whole swap"; web Landing.tsx privacy section

claims.text: The ZEC goes to a shielded address. Its key is split in two halves. (Your browser / The maker)
claims.source: README.md top: spending key split in two halves, the user holds one, the maker the other

claims.text: An escrow on NEAR releases the USDC to whoever reveals the right half. The maker locks USDC first.
claims.source: README.md top and Terms ("Escrow": claim(a) / refund(b)); Landing.tsx FlowDiagram "Locks USDC first"

claims.text: The USDC lands in NEAR Intents under a key made in your browser (gas from the maker). One signature sends it on.
claims.source: README.md top; Terms "Stipend" (0.06 NEAR from the maker to the taker's new NEAR key)
